findings.issue: SignIn() and Recover() filter the CryptoException from KeyWraps.OpenWithPassword / OpenWithRecoveryCode down to `exception.Code is ErrorCode.WrongPassword or ErrorCode.Tampered`. src/Wakeel.Crypto/Keys/KeyWrap.cs throws two further codes from the same call: ErrorCode.Corrupt ("The stored key is missing its derivation settings" when wrap.Kdf is null; "The stored key carries two different salts" when wrap.Salt and wrap.Kdf.Salt disagree) and ErrorCode.UnknownKind (wrap.Version != CurrentVersion, or wrap.Kind != the kind asked for). A keys\admin.key that a half-written save, a hand edit, or a newer build left in any of those states therefore throws straight out of the A02 «دخول» / «استرداد» click handler as an unhandled exception — the screen dies instead of saying «تعذّرت قراءة بيانات الأداة على هذا الحاسوب. افتح «الصيانة» لفحصها.», which AdminAr.Errors.DataUnreadable already exists to say. AdminKeyFile.Load's own CryptoException is caught (TryLoadKeyFile), so the gap is only in the two wrap-opening calls.
findings.fix: In both methods widen the catch to `catch (CryptoException exception)` and branch inside on the code: `exception.Code is ErrorCode.WrongPassword or ErrorCode.Tampered` keeps the current behaviour (RecordWrongPassword(keyFile, now) in SignIn, AdminAccountRefusal.WrongRecoveryCode in Recover); every other code returns `new AdminSignInResult(AdminAccountRefusal.StorageFailed)`, which A02 already renders as AdminAr.Errors.DataUnreadable through its `default:` arm. Add one test per method that corrupts the saved key file (load it, set the password wrap's Version to KeyWrap.CurrentVersion + 1, save) and asserts AdminAccountRefusal.StorageFailed rather than a thrown exception.

findings.issue: TryLoadKeyFile() turns an unreadable key file into null, and SignIn()/Recover() then report AdminAccountRefusal.NotCreated — the same answer as "this computer has no account". A02 reacts by navigating to /first-run; A01.OnInitialized sees Accounts.IsCreated == true (the file exists) and navigates straight back to /sign-in. The person presses «دخول», the screen flickers and returns to itself, and the Arabic sentence written for exactly this case is never shown.
findings.fix: Distinguish absent from unreadable: give AdminAccountService a `KeyFileUnreadable` property (true when AdminKeyFile.Exists(_paths.KeyFile) but TryLoadKeyFile() returns null), and have SignIn()/Recover() return AdminAccountRefusal.StorageFailed instead of NotCreated in that case, so A02's `default:` arm shows AdminAr.Errors.DataUnreadable and stays put. Guard A01.OnInitialized's redirect with the same flag.

findings.issue: PrintAsync() returns AdminPrintOutcome.Saved as soon as CoreWebView2.ShowPrintUI() has opened the system print dialogue — its own XML doc says it "never says what the person then chose". A01CreateAccount.razor then sets _printedAt on that outcome and renders the «طُبعت dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm» chip, so the sheet claims it was printed even when the person cancelled the dialogue. Harmless to the key material (the real gate is the «طبعتُ الورقة» tick box), but the chip states something the tool does not know.
findings.fix: Either rename the outcome to something the service can honestly report (e.g. AdminPrintOutcome.DialogOpened) and drop the timestamp chip, or word the chip as an action rather than a fact — e.g. AdminAr.Account.Create.PrintOpenedChip("فُتحت نافذة الطباعة ١٦:٠١") — so nothing on screen asserts a print that may not have happened.

findings.issue: CopyCode() writes the twenty-one-character organisation recovery code — the second of the only two things that open admin.db and the organisation signing keys — to the Windows clipboard through wakeelAdmin.copyText, with no warning and nothing that clears it. Windows clipboard history (Win+V) and cloud clipboard both retain it long after «ابدأ» has dropped the sheet from UI state, which undoes the care taken everywhere else in this file to hold the code no longer than needed.
findings.fix: Keep the button (the design draws «نسخ الرموز»), but make the toast say what was just done — e.g. «نُسخ الرمز. الصقه في مكانه ثم امسح الحافظة.» — and clear it afterwards: have wakeelAdmin.copyText schedule a navigator.clipboard.writeText('') a short while later, or overwrite the clipboard in Start() when the person leaves A01. At minimum add the sentence.

findings.issue: ReadAlerts() caps each of its three queries at LIMIT 20, and A03Dashboard.razor derives both the WBadge count and AdminAr.Dashboard.AlertsSummary(...) from that capped list. With more than twenty offices waiting, the alerts panel says «٢٠ مكتبًا بانتظار ملف الإعداد» while the «المكاتب المفعّلة» KPI card, which uses the uncapped AdminDashboard.OfficesWaiting, says the true number on the same screen.
findings.fix: Read the three totals separately from the list that is drawn: add three COUNT(*) scalars (offices WHERE activated_at IS NULL, pending_changes WHERE distributed_at IS NULL, devices WHERE revoked_at IS NOT NULL) to AdminDashboard, feed AlertsSummary and the badge from those, and keep the LIMIT 20 for the rendered rows only.

findings.issue: AlertsNoneDesc reads «كل المكاتب لديها ملف إعداد، ولا تغييرات بانتظار التوزيع.» and is shown unconditionally when Alerts.Count == 0. Verified live on a freshly created organisation: the panel claims every office has a setup file on a tool that has no offices at all — the same untruth the offices KPI card already avoids through AdminAr.Dashboard.OfficesWaiting(0, 0).
findings.fix: Give the alerts panel the same two-case treatment: when the board IsEmpty (or Offices == 0) show a description such as «لا شيء بانتظار الانتباه بعد.», and keep the current sentence for a populated organisation.

findings.issue: AlertsSummary and DevicesRevoked build «مُلغاة» onto Counting.Devices(n). For n >= 11 Counting.Count returns the singular «جهازًا», so the line reads «١١ جهازًا مُلغاة» — the adjective should follow the singular noun («مُلغى»), the broken plural «مُلغاة» belonging only to the 3–10 «أجهزة» form.
findings.fix: Give the two call sites a shape-aware helper, e.g. `DevicesRevokedPhrase(int n) => n switch { 1 => "جهاز مُلغى", 2 => "جهازان مُلغيان", >= 3 and <= 10 => $"{n} أجهزة مُلغاة", _ => $"{n} جهازًا مُلغى" }`, and use it in both AlertsSummary and DevicesRevoked instead of concatenating «مُلغاة» onto Counting.Devices.

findings.issue: Recover() writes the new password wrap and calls keyFile.Save(...) before _db.Open(databaseKey). If the open then fails, the method returns AdminAccountRefusal.StorageFailed and A02 shows a generic «تعذّرت قراءة بيانات الأداة», but the password has in fact already been changed — the old password no longer works and nothing on screen told the person so.
findings.fix: Open the database first and save the re-wrapped key file only once it is open (the recovery wrap is unchanged either way, so the printed sheet still works if the save is what fails), or add a refusal whose Arabic says the password was changed but the tool could not be opened.

findings.issue: The host carries `<PackageReference Include="QRCoder" />`, but nothing under src/Wakeel.Admin references QRCoder — the recovery-sheet QR is generated in Wakeel.Admin.UI (AdminRecoveryQr), which has its own reference. A dependency the host does not use.
findings.fix: Delete the QRCoder PackageReference from src/Wakeel.Admin/Wakeel.Admin.csproj; it reaches the output transitively through Wakeel.Admin.UI anyway. (csproj files inside the package's own allowed paths may be edited.)

notes:
BUILD AND TESTS — the four given commands were run verbatim: `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Admin.UI --no-dependencies` (0 warnings / 0 errors), `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Admin --no-dependencies` (0/0), `dotnet build tests/Wakeel.Admin.Tests --no-dependencies` (0/0), `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Admin.Tests --no-build` → Passed! 57 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, duration 6 s. TreatWarningsAsErrors clean.

HOST ACTUALLY RUN AND LOOKED AT — I launched src/Wakeel.Admin/bin/Debug/net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0/Wakeel.Admin.exe myself with --remote-debugging-port=9333 --window-size=1366x768 --data-folder=<scratchpad temp> --start-url=/first-run. http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/version answered (Edg/152.0.4191.66). Python is absent on this machine, so I drove CDP over a PowerShell ClientWebSocket. A01 rendered with all four password rules, Arabic-Indic step chips ١/٢, and the machine line bidi-isolated. I filled the four fields and pressed «إنشاء الحساب والمتابعة»: the once-only red panel, the meta list (تاريخ الإصدار / مدير النظام / رقم الورقة 20260916/25321), the grouped code WXR2-JWXD-PKA9-PHVP-GYSFA and the QR all appeared, and «ابدأ» was gated on the tick box. Ticked, started, and captured A03 through Page.captureScreenshot — I looked at the JPEG: dark top bar with the org line «هيئة تنمية المناطق الريفية · لا دوائر · لا أقسام · لا وحدات», seven tabs, no sidebar, four KPI cards, two panels, full RTL, icons rendering. The log held one line, «Wakeel admin host starting up», and nothing else. I verified on disk that keys\ carries no explicit BUILTIN\Users entry while exports\ carries the non-inherited Modify grant — the narrowed ACL of review pass 1 is real. Process killed; no Wakeel.Admin survives.

SPEC COVERAGE — every item of admin-1 (a) through (e) is present and real: the WPF host with the BlazorWebViewInitializing user-data folder, Serilog file log, validated --remote-debugging-port / --start-url / --window-size / --data-folder (the start-url and port validation against protocol-relative paths and smuggled engine switches is a nice touch), DPAPI protector, print-to-PDF through PrintToPdfAsync; AdminPaths laying ProgramData\WakeelAdmin out exactly as specified; admin.db as its own embedded migration set carrying all nine DATA-MODEL §13 tables; AdminKeyService generating the org Ed25519/X25519 pair and issuing DeviceCertificate.IssueOrgRoot with the seeds sealed under the database key; AdminAccountService with the two Argon2id wraps, the 30 s doubling lock-out after 5 failures (capped at 30 min) held in the key file so a restart cannot clear it, and recovery by code or QR through ZXing; A01/A02/A03 plus AdminConfirmDialog and AdminErrorState from A12; AddWakeelAdmin() delegating to AddAdminAccount() with AdminRoutes pre-declaring A04–A11 behind a Built set and AdminAr split into Common/Account/Dashboard — clean seams for admin-2 and admin-3, which need only add their own AddAdminX() and their own AdminAr partial file.

SECURITY — no secret leak found. The database key is random, never derived from the password, and exists only inside the two wraps; it is wiped in a finally in all three paths, and recoveryCode.KeyMaterial with it. The key file holds only ciphertext plus two non-secret names, asserted by KeyFile_CarriesTwoWrapsAndNoSecretOfItsOwn. admin.db is unopenable with a wrong key and shows neither «SQLite format 3» nor any table name in its raw bytes. The audit writer matches whole name segments and redacts rather than throwing. DPAPI is deliberately not used to wrap admin.db, and AdminDpapiProtector documents exactly why — the right call, and the same reasoning that makes the unbuilt «تذكر هذا الجهاز» tick box the right omission. The remaining security-shaped notes are the clipboard copy (finding 4) and the two error-path findings.

DESIGN FIDELITY — A02 and A03 match their light and dark previews closely. Three deviations, all correctly escalated by the builder as owner decisions rather than silently resolved: (1) the A01 preview draws twelve 8-character one-time codes with no QR, while the specification and Wakeel.Crypto's RecoveryCode define one 21-character code plus QR, and the build follows the specification; (2) the A02 preview carries a «تذكر هذا الجهاز ٨ ساعات» tick box which is not built; (3) the A02 preview's standing note says «١٥ دقيقة بعد ٥ محاولات» where the specification says 30 s doubling. Two smaller, unescalated deviations, both defensible: A01 adds an «اسم الهيئة الكامل» field the preview does not show (the sheet has to print the organisation's name before A04 exists), and the A03 offices KPI shows the bare figure with «من ٦» moved to the sub-line where the preview puts «٤ من ٦» in the value slot.

TESTS — they assert behaviour, not shape: the lock-out test walks four wrong passwords, the fifth, the refusal of the right password during the wait, the clock advance and the doubling; the restart test builds a second service over the same folder; the recovery tests prove the old password stops working, that loose formatting parses, that a stranger's code is refused, and that the sheet survives a password change; the storage tests open the file with a wrong key and grep the raw bytes; the bUnit tests drive A01's two steps and the «ابدأ» gate, A02's attempt counter and lock-out, and A03's alert kinds. No tautologies found. No package outside Directory.Packages.props was added (QRCoder 1.8.0 and ZXing.Net 0.16.11 are both pinned centrally), and nothing outside the package's allowed paths was touched.

VERDICT — one medium finding (the narrow CryptoException filter in SignIn and Recover, a one-line fix in each plus a test) keeps this from an accept. Everything else is low. Fix that one and the package is done.
